chapter: La Rocca and the jazz-origin dispute
title: La Rocca's claim to have started jazz in 1917
summary: Mrs. Laine rejects La Rocca's 1917 claim, citing her grandson's birth and her son Alfred being in New York with Durante.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: I got a swan book there with some... But this is another... Another big liar he's got here. Because she's pointed up. What's that then? In 1917. Ever there was a liar. That's the biggest liar he could ever tell.
He claims he started jazz about 1917.

In 1917. That's one big liar. Because he wasn't even playing music that I remember at that time. That's about when Mr. Wayne Quidditch. And I know when, because my grandson was born in 1917. And he's still living. Lance was born in 1917. Lance.
And that's when he claimed he went to... He went up north with the band. Yeah.
How can you make up the liars?
